structs.name: GfxCmdBuf
structs.size_evidence: NOT PROVEN. Best value 9800 (IDA builder 9800; GfxDrawCallOutput stride 9808). Chain: R_AddDrawCall@0x141971450 writes cmdCount=1 at GfxBackEndData+9808*slot+43528 (`mov dword ptr [rdx+rax+0AA08h], 1`, rdx = 9808*slot via imul 2650h); RB_RunDrawList@0x1419A7D00 and R_FinishImmediateDrawSlot@0x1419A8DC0 read a QWORD at element+33728 and a byte at element+43532. Element base is not a Replay member: if the element starts at 33728 (the QWORD is element+0, the byte is element+9804), cmdCount is at element+9800, which is the end of a 9800-byte GfxCmdBuf when cmdBuf is element+0 and cmdCount directly follows it (game-test order). Lower bound 9769: R_DrawSlot_BindCurrentContext@0x1418E3450 writes byte drawSlot+9768 = 1 (useImmediateContext) on the GfxCmdBuf-typed local. Upper bound 9804: RB_RunDrawList's local drawSlot (`__int64[1225]` = 9800 bytes, frame [rsp+2740h] to next local at [rsp+4D8Ch]) is the object R_DrawSlot_BindCurrentContext initializes. Not closed: element base and element-start identity of the QWORD (its writer was not found in R_DrawShadowMapWorkerSlice or in RB_RunDrawList / R_FinishImmediateDrawSlot / R_ClearAndFlushDrawSlot callers; no further xrefs were traced).
members: R_DrawSlot_BindCurrentContext@0x1418E3450: `*(QWORD *)drawSlot = g_gfxImmediateContext` (8-byte pointer at +0; the Replay value is the immediate context, so the pointer type is UNCONFIRMED)
unconfirmed: cmdBufIndex (IDA +8, 4 bytes), cmdList (IDA +16, ID3D12GraphicsCommandList *): no Replay access found in this pass

descState at +24 with size 9744: arithmetic only. 24 + 9744 = 9768 places useImmediateContext exactly after it; the 9744 size is A184's GfxDescriptorState (R_InitDescriptorState@0x1418791E0, ComputeContextData descState +128 and heapIndex +9872) and belongs to A071 to prove. Game-test descState is 9064, which does not fit the +9768 flag
constantBufferAllocations (24 bytes): after useImmediateContext; 9769 + 24 = 9793, so 7 bytes of padding or a gap are needed to reach 9800 (IDA _pad2381 has 7 bytes already)
total size 9800 vs 9793 + tail: needs the element/cmdCount link above
structs.notes: Not absent: GfxCmdBuf is held by value at +0 of a GfxDrawCallOutput element (A186), and a 9800-byte drawSlot local is a GfxCmdBuf-shaped object with useImmediateContext at +9768. Verdict partial: size bounded 9769..9804 with best 9800; the link that makes 9800 exact is the element base. Coordinator: the GfxBackEndData element base (33728) equals 33372 + 4*89, the per-worker int array (`[rax+rdi*4+825Ch]` in R_AddDrawCall) if its slot count is 89. The 89 is the game-test count (drawOutput[89]), NOT yet verified in Replay, so treat the base as a candidate. Owner decision needed on GfxDrawCallOutput (proposal below) before GfxCmdBuf can be resolved.

structs.name: GfxVertexBufferState
structs.size_evidence: NOT PROVEN. IDA 72 and builder 112 are priors only. Replay evidence: R_CreateDynamicBuffers@0x1418DA6E0 'mayhemChannelsVbPool' loop writes a 168-byte element (`v2 += 42` DWORDs, `memset_0(v2, 0, 0xA8)`) with `v2[0] = 0` (used, +0) and `v2[1] = 278528` (total, +4), and calls R_GfxWrappedBuffer_AllocateWithFlag20 with `v2 + 2` (+8, the wrapped buffer, not an ID3D12Resource* pointer), R_CreateDynamicUploadBuffer at +40, the device resource at +120 (`*((_QWORD *)v2 + 15)`), and SubmitDwordBinding/SubmitDwordRange at +104 and +136. So the Replay pool element is 168 bytes and its +8 member is a wrapped buffer, which does not match game-test's buffer pointer at +8. The pool element is typed GfxVertexBufferState in game-test (GfxBuffers.mayhemChannelsVbPool 144 = 2 x 72).
members: R_CreateDynamicBuffers@0x1418DA6E0: `v2[0] = 0` in the mayhem pool element (stride 168, game-test pool element GfxVertexBufferState)
R_CreateDynamicBuffers@0x1418DA6E0: `v2[1] = 278528` (same element); the wrapped allocation size 0x44000 = 278528 agrees
changed_members: Replay has the wrapped buffer at +8 (R_GfxWrappedBuffer_AllocateWithFlag20 target `v2 + 2`); the device resource is stored at +120, not +8
Replay wrapped target is +8 with the 64-byte IDA GfxWrappedBuffer (Replay copies +8..+24 to +72 and +24..+40 to +88); not +16 with 56
unconfirmed: Whether the 168-byte Replay pool element is one GfxVertexBufferState (size 168, method 4 by the array stride) or a larger struct that contains a GfxVertexBufferState at +0 (size 72 with 96 trailing bytes, where 96 = GfxWrappedRWBuffer in IDA). Both fit the code; neither is proven

GfxVertexBufferState used by Replay elsewhere: R_InitCmdBufState / R_CmdBuf_BindZeroVertexBuffers32 touch only GfxCmdBufState (A185): no proof for the dynamic VB (+0x11B0 pointer target is the global s_cmdBufStateBlock, not this struct)

R_ToggleSmpFrameInternal (game-test: frontEndDataOut->mayhemChannelsVb = &gfxBuf.mayhemChannelsVbPool[frame]) is not read in Replay in this pass; that would show whether the pool element is used as a VB view
structs.notes: Partial. Replay shows used/total at +0/+4 on the mayhem pool element (confirmed), but the element stride 168 and the +8 wrapped-buffer target contradict the 72-byte game-test layout. Do not apply 112 or 72: the owner should decide the pool element type (GfxBuffers owner, A071/A185 range) first. Proposal for the coordinator: the GfxBuffers mayhemChannelsVbPool element is 168 bytes in Replay (stride), not 72; GfxVertexBufferState as game-test defines it may be wrong for this pool.

proposals_for_other_owners.proposal: element stride 9808 is CONFIRMED (R_AddDrawCall and RB_RunDrawList arithmetic). Candidate layout if element base = GfxBackEndData+33728: finished QWORD +0 (read, cleared in RB_RunDrawList and R_FinishImmediateDrawSlot), cmdBuf +0 of 9800 bytes (GfxCmdBuf candidate), cmdCount +9800, empty bool +9804, tail 3 bytes. Game-test has cmdCount at 9120 and inCmdCount/empty after it; Replay has no inCmdCount access found (R_AddDrawCall's per-slot int at 33372 is a separate array). Size 9808 proposal (IDA 9136). Needs the element base proof (a write of the element+0 QWORD or a count-89 check), then owner decision.

per-worker int array at +33372 (`[rax+rdi*4+825Ch]`, 4-byte flags written in R_AddDrawCall and read in RB_RunDrawList / R_FinishImmediateDrawSlot). If the array has 89 entries it ends exactly at 33728, which is the candidate element base for GfxDrawCallOutput above. Count 89 not verified in Replay.
